delivery_semantics.consumer: Explicit partition ownership, unique per-session group, manual commits after SQLite transaction commit
delivery_semantics.guarantee: At least once with idempotent persistence; no distributed exactly-once claim
delivery_semantics.producer: acks=all, idempotence, five in-flight requests, 500 pending futures, 30-second delivery timeout; no application resends
delivery_semantics.restart: Graceful consumer restart from group committed offsets; producer continuation under the same UUID is rejected

limitations: One broker and replication factor one provide no high availability.
Local plaintext listener, not production authentication/TLS.
Kafka/SQLite do not share an atomic transaction; at-least-once delivery is explicit.
Fatal schema/delivery errors remain failures; producer resume is deliberately disabled.
Kafka retention can remove old broker records; SQLite histories also require deliberate disk management.
Measured transport throughput is a laptop observation, not scheduler performance or a statistical benchmark.
Timed test covers only the first 250 authentic arrivals at 600x; it is explicitly partial.
No Phase 5 live dashboard page, final academic report or presentation is implemented.

metrics.consumed: Durably accepted valid deliveries, including exact duplicates; failed invalid batches are not counted as accepted.
metrics.demand: Offered CPU/memory request sums and logical-time arrival buckets, not allocated resources/utilization.
metrics.lag: Observed topic-partition lag is separate from producer-boundary session lag.
metrics.recent_throughput: Distinct accepted instances in the last ten wall-clock seconds / 10.
metrics.throughput_denominator: Distinct persisted instances divided by session wall elapsed seconds through final verification, excluding broker startup and pre-session setup.
